This role ensures secure and highly available connectivity, and leads delivery of high-impact initiatives with measurable outcomes. The ideal candidate has a results-driven mindset, deep operational rigor, and a proven track record of executing complex network programs end-to-end. Key Responsibilities Design and deliver scalable, resilient Data Center, Campus Network solutions using Cisco, Arista, HPE, and Aruba platforms. Support WAN operations such as internet edge, and SD-WAN integrations with consistent routing and security posture. Lead complex troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, and implement preventive changes to prevent incidents and unscheduled outages. Partner with various teams such as Data Center, Storage, Virtualization, Windows, Unix, Cloud Ops, and Security to provide technical direction and deliver cross-domain programs Establish and maintain network documentation, diagrams, standards, and runbooks; ensure designs are supportable and operationally ready. Operationalize delivered solutions for Day 2 operations, including monitoring/alerting, capacity planning, lifecycle management, and change/release processes. Provide clear, timely status, risks, and tradeoffs to stakeholders; manage deliverables, timelines, and dependencies across multiple initiatives. Required Skills 12+ years of hands-on experience designing, deploying, and operating enterprise networks using Cisco/Arista and Aruba (wired/wireless) platforms. Expert-level routing and switching knowledge (BGP, OSPF, EVPN/VXLAN), high availability (MLAG/vPC, LACP), and data center networking design patterns. Strong background in network security fundamentals (segmentation, ACLs, firewall integrations, secure remote access) and partnering with Security teams on controls and audits. Hands-on experience with NAC/AAA solutions including Cisco ISE and/or Aruba ClearPass. Experience with SD-WAN design/operations and hybrid connectivity patterns is a strong plus. Experience supporting Cisco VPN, Aruba ClearPass, F5 Load Balancer is a plus. Experience with network automation and observability (e.g., scripting, templating, telemetry, monitoring/alerting) to improve reliability and reduce MTTR. Exceptional problem-solving and analytical skills with disciplined incident, change, and risk management practices. Strong communication skills, able to translate technical details into executive-ready updates, options, and recommendations. Thrives in dynamic environments with the ability to prioritize, manage ambiguity, and drive outcomes across competing business needs. Qualification 12–15 years of experience in enterprise network architecture, design, deployment, and operations (data center, campus, WAN and hybrid cloud). Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field. Cisco certification required (CCNP preferred; CCIE a strong plus). We’re doing work that matters. Help us solve what others can’t.

review_candidates.title: MEL Advisor
review_candidates.description: A propos de FHI 360: FHI 360 est une organisation à but non lucratif dédiée au développement humain qui s'engage à améliorer durablement les conditions de vie en proposant des solutions intégrées et adaptées au contexte local. Notre personnel comprend des experts dans les domaines de la santé, des menaces pour la santé publique, de l'éducation, de la nutrition, de l'environnement, du développement économique, de la société civile, de la jeunesse, de la recherche, de la technologie, de la communication et du marketing social, créant ainsi un ensemble unique de compétences pour relever les défis interdépendants du développement actuel. Le programme Global Health Security (GHS) du gouvernement américain (USG) fournit une aide vitale pour prévenir, détecter et répondre aux menaces de maladies infectieuses qui présentent des risques pour la santé publique et pourraient coûter des vies. Dans le cadre du programme GHS de l'USG, l'activité Strengthening Infectious disease Détection Systems (STRIDES) fait progresser les efforts intersectoriels visant à identifier, gérer et répondre avec succès aux menaces de maladies infectieuses, à détecter et prévenir de nouvelles épidémies, et à instaurer la confiance dans les structures et les services de détection et de surveillance des maladies d'un pays. À Madagascar, STRIDES contribue également au renforcement des systèmes de surveillance et de réponse en lien avec la santé maternelle, néonatale et infantile (MNCH), notamment en matière de mortalité et de nutrition, ainsi qu’au soutien des efforts d’éradication de la poliomyélite, à travers l’intégration des activités de surveillance, d’investigation et de riposte, conformément aux priorités de la sécurité sanitaire mondiale. Résumé du poste : Le conseiller en suivi, évaluation et apprentissage (MEL Advisor) fournit des conseils techniques sur tous les aspects MEL de l'activité STRIDES (renforcement des systèmes de détection des maladies infectieuses) en Madagascar, notamment en supervisant l'exécution des activités MEL quotidiennes, en élaborant et en mettant en œuvre des politiques et des processus, et en garantissant la qualité des services fournis à l'aide des données du projet afin d'assurer une prise de décision fondée sur des preuves. Il/elle dirigera les activités visant à développer, opérationnaliser, mettre en œuvre et gérer les systèmes, outils et procédures MEL afin de collecter, compiler, analyser, interpréter et utiliser les données qui démontrent l'impact, la responsabilité et les progrès de l'activité. Le conseiller MEL supervisera directement le STRIDES MEL Officer et indirectement le personnel technique et les sous-traitants au niveau national afin de s'assurer que les activités menées dans le pays sont conformes aux objectifs du plan de travail et au plan MEL de l'activité (AMELP) et, par extension, aux priorités du gouvernement américain, et qu'elles sont mises en œuvre avec la plus grande qualité, dans les délais et dans les limites du budget. De plus, le titulaire de ce poste travaillera en étroite collaboration avec le personnel de PATH, sous-partenaire de STRIDES, basé à Madagascar. Le conseiller MEL fera la promotion de STRIDES en tant que leader d'opinion au sein de la communauté MEL en Côte d'Ivoire, contribuant ainsi au leadership éclairé de FHI 360 dans ce domaine grâce à la documentation des meilleures pratiques. Responsabilités: Soutenir la conception, le développement, la planification, la mise en œuvre et le reporting du plan AMELP de STRIDES. Développer, opérationnaliser, mettre en œuvre et gérer les systèmes, outils et procédures MEL afin de collecter, compiler, analyser, interpréter et utiliser les données qui démontrent l'impact, la responsabilité et les progrès des activités. Suivre les progrès du programme STRIDES par rapport aux indicateurs et aux objectifs MEL afin d'assurer un suivi et un reporting cohérents et systématiques. Veiller à ce que les plans MEL pertinents intègrent des méthodes quantitatives et qualitatives de haute qualité et des méthodologies participatives afin de contrôler la qualité des projets en termes de performances et de résultats. Évaluer les données et les efforts de reporting des sous-traitants en matière de MEL afin d'en vérifier la qualité. Renforcer les capacités du personnel de STRIDES en matière de MEL, notamment en renforçant, gérant et mettant en œuvre les systèmes MEL, en assurant la qualité des données, en facilitant l'apprentissage et l'échange de connaissances, en documentant les leçons apprises et les meilleures pratiques, et en établissant des rapports. Diriger les activités d'apprentissage et l'initiative d'utilisation des données de STRIDES ; favoriser une culture d'apprentissage et de partage des connaissances. Gérer les relations dans le pays avec les homologues des gouvernements nationaux, régionaux et locaux et les partenaires multisectoriels dans le domaine du MEL ; identifier le soutien technique nécessaire pour atteindre les objectifs nationaux en matière de sécurité sanitaire mondiale et de MEL. Diriger l'élaboration de plans et de budgets MEL spécifiques à chaque pays, alignés sur les objectifs de STRIDES et garantissant la conformité avec les politiques et procédures des donateurs et de l'organisation. Identifier et consulte l'équipe de direction de STRIDES sur les recommandations visant à améliorer la mise en œuvre et les résultats des activités. Superviser et encadrer le personnel ; supervise les processus de recrutement, d'embauche et d'intégration selon les besoins. Soutenir la gestion des performances et le développement professionnel des subordonnés directs, notamment par le biais de retours d'information réguliers, de coaching et d'accompagnement de carrière. Accomplir d'autres tâches qui lui sont assignées. Connaissances et compétences appliquées : Connaissance approfondie et expérience des mécanismes dans le domaine des pratiques nationales et internationales en matière de suivi, d'évaluation et d'apprentissage (MEL). Capacité à gérer des projets, à établir des priorités réalistes et à planifier la mise en œuvre réussie des activités. Excellentes compétences en communication orale et écrite ; maîtrise d'une deuxième langue (français, espagnol et/ou russe) souhaitable. Excellentes compétences organisationnelles et analytiques. Leadership technique et en matière de projets démontré. Capacité à motiver, influencer et bien travailler avec les autres pour atteindre les objectifs de STRIDES. Capacité à échanger des informations, à présenter des recommandations et à collaborer avec des collègues et des pairs au sein de STRIDES et à l'extérieur, selon les besoins. Capacité à convaincre les autres des avantages/de l'importance d'une idée ou d'un plan d'action et à obtenir leur soutien ou leur engagement. Solides compétences en matière de négociation et capacité à parvenir à des points d'accord et à des avantages mutuels entre pairs et collègues. Capacité à établir des relations de travail positives avec diverses communautés de parties prenantes, des représentants gouvernementaux et d'autres organismes multilatéraux et représentants de donateurs. Solides compétences organisationnelles, grand souci du détail et efficacité dans le respect des délais. Compétences : Il existe beaucoup des compétences de développement FHI 360, les plus axées pour ce poste particulier seront : Gestion de projet (planification et gestion du temps) Définir précisément la durée et la difficulté des tâches (définir objectifs/objectifs/mesures). Divise le travail en étapes, plannings, tâches et affectations de personnes. Organise efficacement les personnes, le temps et les ressources. Organise l'information de manière utile et orchestre plusieurs activités en même temps. Gestion des Personnes (Rendre les Autres Grands) Faciliter le développement professionnel du personnel en proposant des missions et opportunités stimulantes et apprenantes. Il partage et sollicite des retours au moins chaque mois. Aide à établir des plans de développement convaincants. Attribue la responsabilité et la responsabilité des tâches/décisions. Surveille le processus, l'avancement et les résultats. Cela crée un climat où les gens veulent donner le meilleur d'eux-mêmes. Création et gestion de systèmes et de processus. Reconnaît la nécessité de normalisation et équilibre les besoins du client et de l'organisation dans la conception des systèmes. Anticipe les effets du changement de processus sur les personnes tout en optimisant l'efficacité et la simplicité des tâches. Les employés sont censés posséder ou avoir un fort potentiel pour le développement de ces trois compétences fondamentales. Résolution de problèmes et impact : Démontre la capacité d'évaluer les besoins dans le cadre des devoirs convenus et considère la meilleure marche à suivre pour répondre à ces besoins. Applique efficacement les connaissances du domaine technique pour résoudre un large éventail de problèmes. Démontre la capacité à développer des solutions à des problèmes qui ne peuvent être résolus avec les méthodes ou approches existantes. Des décisions/recommandations erronées/échecs à accomplir des missions entraînent généralement de sérieux retards dans les projets assignés, entraînant une dépense considérable de temps, de ressources et de fonds supplémentaires. Les décisions et actions impactent principalement le flux de travail, les processus de projet et les délais. Les problèmes rencontrés sont variés, nécessitant une révision des pratiques et des précédents pour être résolus. La résolution de problèmes consiste à évaluer et résoudre les écarts de données, d'analyses, de processus, etc., dans le cadre des directives prescrites. Des politiques ou des directives existent pour la plupart des problèmes ; d'autres doivent être orientés par un superviseur ou un professionnel plus expérimenté. Supervision accordée/reçue : Peut superviser des membres du personnel subalternes. Coordonne son propre flux de travail et fixe ses priorités individuelles. Travaille selon les directives générales en matière d'achèvement et d'exactitude déterminées par le superviseur. Obtenir des résultats par l'intermédiaire de cadres subalternes ou de collaborateurs expérimentés qui exercent leur indépendance dans leurs missions. Sert de mentor au personnel technique moins expérimenté. Relève du directeur du projet STRIDES à Madagascar. Éducation : ** ** Maîtrise ou équivalent international en services de la connaissance/de l'information, biostatistique, épidémiologie, communication, santé, sciences comportementales, sciences de la vie/sciences sociales, développement international, développement humain ou dans un domaine connexe. Exigences physiques typiques : Environnement de bureau typique. Capacité à passer de longues heures devant un écran d'ordinateur et à faire du travail répétitif sur un clavier. review_candidates.title: UN Women - Regional Programme Specialist, P4, Panama City, Panama FTA
review_candidates.description: Job Description Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. In order to contribute to this result, the UN Women Regional Office for the Americas and the Caribbean, in collaboration with the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID) implements the project "Transforming economies. Towards the Recognition, Reduction and Redistribution of Unpaid Domestic and Care Work in Latin America and the Caribbean". The objective of the project is to increase the economic autonomy and well-being of women in Latin America through their access to comprehensive care policies and systems. To this end, at the regional level, the project works on the generation of applicable knowledge and public positioning on comprehensive care policies and systems in Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC). At the national level, the project is implemented in Peru, Ecuador, Mexico, Panama and the Dominican Republic, strengthening national and local capacities to provide care services and infrastructures at the national and subnational level as an impetus towards the construction of a National Care System, placing special emphasis on the generation of inspiring practices at the local level. Likewise, in its mission, the project seeks to strengthen bi-regional cooperation between Latin America and the Caribbean with Europe, taking advantage of the impulse that feminist foreign policy in both regions is giving to the development of comprehensive care policies and systems. Under the guidance and direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director, the Regional Programme Specialist will be responsible for providing strategic leadership and comprehensive management of the care program. The incumbent will substantively and operationally coordinate the implementation of programmed care activities, ensure effective articulation between the different components of the project, and ensure the achievement of results and implementation of activities in accordance with the Project Document approved by UN Women and the donor and other applicable reference documents. The Regional Programme Specialist will work closely with the economic empowerment team, specifically the technical care specialists and operations team of the UN Women regional office, as well as the economic empowerment teams of the UN Women country offices in Latin America and the Caribbean. Likewise, in coordination with UN Women's country offices, the incumbent will maintain communication with national and local partner institutions to ensure the implementation of the activities foreseen in the project in the prioritized countries and contribute to the development of regional activities and the achievement of results. Availability is required for travel within Latin America and the Caribbean. Key Functions and Accountabilities : Lead the implementation of the project "Transforming economies. Towards the Recognition, reduction and redistribution of unpaid domestic and care work in Latin America and the Caribbean" at the LAC regional level Lead the implementation of activities developed under the regional component of the care project, ensuring high standards of quality and efficiency and fostering synergies between regional, national, and local components. This includes the coordination, monitoring and substantive review of the products and actions developed in the field of care. Lead strategic project planning and collaborate with country offices to develop and implement Annual Work Plans, evaluating progress, budget execution and results, and providing technical guidance for efficient management. Establish and strengthen coordination mechanisms between the countries involved in the program and the levels of work, including the subnational level (local governments, civil society, among others), to ensure fluid communication and effective articulation of actions; Contribute to the establishment and strengthening of strategic alliances with institutional partners and key actors, create synergies with other donor initiatives in the region, and broaden the base of collaboration through consultation and mapping processes of relevant actors in the care agenda. Facilitate inter-agency relations between UN Women and its partners through planning, coordination, and active participation in dialogue spaces such as technical meetings, workshops, field missions, and other related events; Maintain a channel of permanent consultation and coordination with the technical teams of the country offices, the specialized technical advisors, the UN Women regional team, national and/or local partners and the donor, to contribute to the articulated implementation of the project activities; Coordinate the organization and governance mechanisms of the Project (Regional Steering Committee, National Steering Committee and Operational Working Group) and provide relevant technical inputs such as presentations, key data, executive reports and supporting documentation; Collaborate in the implementation of communication and advocacy strategies to make visible the results of the project and the work of UN Women in care, providing technical inputs for communication products, and defend the care agenda in key spaces at the regional level; Lead the design and implementation of the project's monitoring and evaluation strategy, develop tools for monitoring results and indicators, evaluate the impact of activities, and oversee the preparation of technical and financial reports in accordance with UN Women and donor standards. Plan, organize and participate in missions, events, workshops and other activities related to the area of care promoted by UN Women or other partners; Advise ACRO management and country offices on project execution, providing technical inputs to support decision-making and the quality of interventions; Respond to any other requests or requirements from the UN Women regional office or in relation to the implementation of the project or the work of UN Women at the regional level. Provide technical advisory support on UN Women's actions in the field of care at the regional level within the framework of the care project in LAC. Provide specialized technical advice to country offices, government partners, and civil society organizations to develop and/or strengthen care systems, policies, frameworks, and strategies in the region. Develop context analysis, programmatic proposals, and methodological tools that contribute to evidence-based policymaking, as well as resource mobilization around the care agenda. Collaborate in the organization and facilitation of spaces for dialogue, meetings and face-to-face and virtual workshops, aimed at different strategic actors, in order to expand the processes of training, learning and articulation in the region. Manage the production and review of technical knowledge (policy documents, guides, case studies, tools, etc.), and evaluate experiences developed by UN Women in the region, ensuring their articulation with the regional care agenda. Create mechanisms for dialogue and participation with key actors to defend the political and technical commitment to the implementation of comprehensive care systems, in line with the Tlatelolco Commitment and other regional initiatives. Manage the development of partnerships and resource mobilization as it relates to the care project in LAC. Provide technical support and guidance to MCO and COs on managing activities and other promotional events to engage bilateral and multilateral institutions/donors, private sector and civil society to expand and/or sustain interest and resources for UN Women programmes and joint UN system programmes; As part of strategic planning, provide support and advice to MCO and COs in forging and implementing strategic partnerships to increase UN Women’s positioning in country; Liaise with key stakeholders from Government, academia, civil society, the private sector and key international actors to build and strengthen strategic alliances and partnerships on women’s rights and gender equality initiatives. Facilitate knowledge building and sharing within the framework of the care project in LAC. Support and oversee the reporting and produce regional analysis including global trends and identifying challenges. Lead the development and dissemination of good practices and lessons learned on coordination and gender mainstreaming. Provide capacity development support to regional and country level colleagues on coordination mandate and gender mainstreaming. Develop capacity development initiatives on gender-related issues and priorities as needed. The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization. Competencies : Core Values: Integrity; Professionalism; Respect for Diversity. Core Competencies: Awareness and Sensitivity Regarding Gender Issues; Accountability; Creative Problem Solving; Effective Communication; Inclusive Collaboration; Stakeholder Engagement; Leading by Example. Please visit this link for more information on UN Women’s Values and Competencies Framework: Functional Competencies: Excellent knowledge of gender equality and women’s empowerment issues Excellent knowledge of UN system and understanding of inter-agency coordination processes Ability to think innovatively; Ability to conduct policy research and knowledge products; Ability to interact with donors, identify and analyze trends, opportunities and threats to fundraising; Ability to advocate and advise on policy. Excellent knowledge of program development and delivery, results-based management, and reporting. Recruitment Qualifications : Education: Master’s degree or equivalent in international development, public administration, public policy, economy, international cooperation, or other relevant social science field is required. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Experience: At least 7 years of progressively responsible experience in the design, implementation, coordination and evaluation of gender equality strategies and agendas, policies and programmes is required. Experience related to gender equality and women’s rights, especially in care policies and social protection, is required. Experience in leading and coaching staff in international settings is required. Experience working with international organizations and/or in development cooperation in Latin America and the Caribbean region is required. Additional Experience in other regions is desirable. Experience in mobilizing resources and managing strategic partnerships with governments, international organizations, civil society, academia, and donors is required. Experience working in developing countries within the UN system, Agencies, Funds or Programs is desirable. Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.), spreadsheet and database packages is required. Experience in the use of a modern web-based ERP System, preferably Oracle Cloud, is desirable. Languages : Fluency in English and Spanish is required. Fluency in Portuguese is desirable Knowledge of another official UN language is desirable (French, Arabic, Chinese, or Russian) Statements : In July 2010, the United Nations General Assembly created UN Women, the United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women. The creation of UN Women came about as part of the UN reform agenda, bringing together resources and mandates for greater impact. It merges and builds on the important work of four previously distinct parts of the UN system (DAW, OSAGI, INSTRAW and UNIFEM), which focused exclusively on gender equality and women's empowerment. Diversity and inclusion: At UN Women, we are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. UN Women recruits, employs, trains, compensates, and promotes regardless of race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, ability, national origin, or any other basis covered by appropriate law. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, competence, integrity and organizational need. If you need any reasonable accommodation to support your participation in the recruitment and selection process, please include this information in your application. UN Women has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UN Women, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination. All selected candidates will be expected to adhere to UN Women’s policies and procedures and the standards of conduct expected of UN Women personnel and will therefore undergo rigorous reference and background checks. (Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check.) Note: Applicants must ensure that all sections of the application form, including the sections on education and employment history, are completed. If all sections are not completed the application may be disqualified from the recruitment and selection process .

review_candidates.title: Global Financial Shared Services Manager
review_candidates.description: Job Summary The Global Financial Shared Services Manager will lead IPA's newly established Shared Services Center within the Global Finance team. The role is responsible for building the center from the ground up — designing processes, developing a team of up to five staff, and serving as the primary point of contact for country office finance teams and headquarters leadership. The Shared Services Manager will ensure timely, accurate, and compliant processing of accounts payable, journal entries, expense reports, intercompany transactions, and bank and balance sheet reconciliations across all IPA entities worldwide. Responsibilities Operations and Service Delivery Lead day-to-day operations of the Shared Services Center, covering accounts payable, journal entry processing, intercompany transactions, and bank and balance sheet reconciliations for all IPA offices. Establish and monitor service-level agreements (SLAs) with country offices and headquarters, including processing turnaround times, accuracy rates, and query resolution timelines. Coordinate with country office finance staff to resolve queries, address missing documentation, clear reconciliation discrepancies, and ensure completeness of month-end close activities. Provide coverage to country office finance teams during periods of staff transition. Support all offices with audit requests as needed. Process Design and Continuous Improvement Identify opportunities for automation, system improvements, and process simplification, and lead implementation in coordination with IT and Global Finance teams. Develop performance dashboards and key performance indicators (KPIs) for the Shared Services function, and report results to senior finance leadership on a regular cadence. Build team capacity to take on additional responsibilities with a consistent level of excellence. Team Leadership and Talent Development Recruit, onboard, and supervise a team of up to three Shared Services staff. Set individual performance objectives, conduct performance reviews, and support professional development. Design and deliver training for junior staff on accounting tasks, reconciliation procedures, NetSuite operations, and country-specific requirements; maintain training documentation for knowledge continuity. Monitor individual and team workload across country assignments; adjust capacity allocation and escalate resourcing needs proactively. Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Compliance and Controls Ensure all transactions comply with IPA policies, donor requirements, and relevant accounting standards. Support internal and external audits by providing required documentation. Maintain clear segregation of duties between the Shared Services Center and country office banking and treasury functions. Stakeholder Engagement and Reporting Serve as the primary liaison between the Shared Services Center, country office finance teams, and headquarters Global Finance. Oversee generation of monthly financial reports for distribution to country office finance teams and leadership. Lead regular check-ins and reporting meetings with country office finance leads, providing updates on month-end close status, outstanding issues, and team performance. Communicate process changes, training requirements, and service updates to all stakeholders. Contribute to cross-functional projects related to finance transformation and other global initiatives as needed. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in accounting or finance. Minimum seven years of progressive experience in accounting, including at least three years of direct supervisory experience. Demonstrated experience leading or working in a shared services, business process outsourcing (BPO), or centralized finance environment. Full professional proficiency in English and Spanish, written and spoken. Strong working knowledge of accounts payable processes, general ledger accounting, and internal controls. Proficiency with ERP systems, preferably NetSuite, and advanced Microsoft Excel skills. Proven ability to collaborate across time zones and cultures, with strong written and verbal communication skills. Experience supporting multi-currency and multi-country accounting operations. Certified Public Accountant (CPA), Chartered Accountant (CA), or equivalent professional certification. (preferred) Master's degree in accounting, finance, or business administration. (preferred) Experience with nonprofit, international development, or donor-funded organizations, including familiarity with USG and FCDO requirements. (preferred) Demonstrated experience designing or improving accounting processes across multiple entities or geographies. (preferred) Location This role may be based in any IPA office, provided a high level of overlap with other offices' time zones. Reports To Global Controller (Headquarters) Application Deadline 1 Oct 2026 About IPA Innovations for Poverty Action (IPA) is a research and policy nonprofit that discovers and advances what works to improve the lives of people living in poverty. IPA brings together researchers and decision-makers to design, rigorously evaluate, and refine these solutions and their applications, ensuring that the evidence created is used to improve the lives of people living in poverty. In recent decades, trillions of dollars have been spent on programs designed to reduce global poverty, but clear evidence of which programs succeed is rare, and when evidence does exist, decision-makers often do not know about it. IPA exists to bring together leading researchers and these decision-makers to ensure that the evidence we create leads to a tangible impact on the world. Since its founding in 2002, IPA has worked with over 600 leading academics to conduct over 1,000 evaluations in 52 countries. This research has informed hundreds of successful programs that now impact millions of individuals worldwide. Safeguarding at IPA At Innovations for Poverty Action (IPA), we are committed to creating a safe and respectful environment for all individuals, particularly children and vulnerable adults. As IPA adheres to strict safeguarding principles, selected candidates will be expected to adhere to these standards. By joining IPA, you become part of a team dedicated to ethical conduct, social responsibility, and meaningful impact in the fight against global poverty. Together, we work to create a better world where everyone has the opportunity to thrive with dignity and respect.

Support marketing technology audits. Support project management activities using Monday.com. Research industry trends and incorporate digital marketing best practices to inform strategy. Assist in the documentation of unit processes that support workflows or address challenges. review_candidates.title: DL3 Realty - Chief Investment & Growth Officer
review_candidates.description: Organization Overview: DL3 Realty DL3 Realty is a Chicago-based real estate development and investment firm with a 25-year track record of advancing catalytic projects across housing, retail, healthcare, education, industrial, office, and mixed-use real estate. The firm has shaped a sophisticated platform that brings together private capital, public partners, anchor institutions, community leaders, lenders, investors, and operating partners to pursue opportunities that conventional investors have often overlooked. At the center of DL3's approach is Venture Development™, a nationally recognized, place-based investment framework grounded in disciplined real estate judgment, public-private partnership, community engagement, and strategic timing. The approach identifies places where perception may lag fundamentals and where deliberate investment can generate attractive risk-adjusted returns while strengthening the conditions for broader economic growth. The firm’s 2020 Neighborhood Impact Portfolio has demonstrated that thesis across Chicago. The firm's work has included adaptive reuse, retail, healthcare, industrial development, and affordable and mixed-income housing - often using complex capital stacks that combine private investment with tools such as tax credits, TIF, and other public-private financing. Since 2020 alone, DL3 has invested more than $250 million dollars to develop more than one million square feet of commercial real estate and create more than 3,000 permanent jobs. Today, DL3 is extending that model to downtown Chicago. The firm believes the Loop's structural transition creates an opportunity to reposition underutilized assets and help evolve the central business district into a more vibrant place to live, work, learn, and build a life. ACōDA at Pritzker Park - a planned $162 million, 300-unit mixed-income development - and the $270 million adaptive reuse of 135 South LaSalle into 394 mixed-income apartments are early expressions of that strategy. You can learn more by visiting their website at: https://www.dl3realty.com/ Role Summary: Chief Investment & Growth Officer DL3 Realty is seeking a Chief Investment & Growth Officer (CIGO) to partner closely with CEO Leon I. Walker and the senior leadership team to help lead the firm's further evolution into an institutional investment enterprise. The CIGO will play a defining role in shaping the strategy, platform, and capabilities that position DL3 for its next generation of growth. The CIGO will bring the investment judgment, capital connectivity, institutional sophistication, and enterprise leadership required to turn DL3's proven track record into a scalable investment platform. Working alongside DL3’s experienced real estate and development team, the CIGO will help translate opportunities into executable investment strategies and build the capabilities required to scale the business. A central mandate will be capital formation. DL3's objective is to secure new institutional equity commitments and build relationships capable of supporting multiple generations of projects and investment vehicles. As a member of the leadership team, the CIGO will expand DL3's investor network and take opportunities from relationship-building through diligence, structuring, negotiation, and close. Many senior investment executives are asked to manage an established platform. DL3 offers something different: the opportunity to help build one. The CIGO will connect capital, investments, people, systems, and strategy to help scale the firm and pursue increasingly ambitious opportunities, with Chicago as the immediate focus and the potential to extend DL3's model into additional markets over time. Key Responsibilities: Capital Formation & Investor Partnerships Develop and execute a capital formation strategy aligned with DL3’s investment priorities and growth objectives. Build trusted relationships with family offices, private investors, wealth platforms, institutional investors, and strategic partners. Lead investor engagement from introduction through diligence, structuring, negotiation, and close, cultivating anchor commitments and repeat capital. Evaluate and help structure investment vehicles, including funds, joint ventures, co-investments, and other structures, to support DL3’s growth. Investment Strategy, Acquisitions & Deal-Making Partner with the CEO and leadership team to shape portfolio strategy, investment priorities, risk parameters, and capital allocation. Evaluate acquisitions, dispositions, and new investment opportunities aligned with DL3’s Venture Development™ framework. Bring rigor to underwriting and investment decisions, including capital structures, market assumptions, risk, returns, and exit strategies. Develop creative capital solutions that leverage private investment, debt, public incentives, and other sources while maintaining investment discipline. Lead key investment decisions and negotiations in partnership with DL3’s real estate and development team. Executive Leadership & Culture Serve as a senior member of DL3's leadership team, investment committee, and a close partner to the CEO on firm strategy, investments, capital, talent, and growth. Provide day-to-day leadership to the development team and help translate entrepreneurial ideas and new opportunities into disciplined execution. Model a culture of excellence, urgency, curiosity, humility, teamwork, and follow-through. Present and lead advisory board meetings, investor communications and pipeline reporting. Institutionalization & Operating Discipline Help ensure strong systems, governance, processes, and culture for the growth strategy for DL3 Lead a seamless institutional investor experience from first contact through diligence, closing, reporting, distributions, and repeat investment. Partner across finance, accounting, legal, development, asset management, and operations to ensure investment decisions are supported by reliable information and clear accountability. Identify the systems, capabilities, talent, and practices required to support DL3’s growth strategy. Civic & Market Leadership Represent DL3 with sophistication and credibility in investor meetings, family office gatherings, real estate forums, civic settings, and industry events. Understand that DL3's investment strategy is inseparable from Chicago's civic and economic future, and participate meaningfully in the relationships and conversations shaping the city. Translate DL3's track record, Chicago thesis, risk profile, and impact into a compelling institutional narrative for investors and partners. The Ideal Candidate The ideal candidate will be a sophisticated investment and growth leader, relationship builder, and strategic operator who is energized by the opportunity to help scale an entrepreneurial business. While no single candidate will bring every attribute, strong candidates will demonstrate: Capital Connectivity + Investment Judgment: Brings strong financial and investment judgment, credibility with sophisticated capital partners, and the ability to turn relationships into committed capital. Understands how to assess risk, return, structure, and strategic fit. Institutional + Entrepreneurial Mindset: Brings institutional sophistication while thriving in a lean, fast-moving environment. Knows how to introduce greater rigor, systems, and discipline without sacrificing creativity, speed, or entrepreneurial thinking. Builder + Growth Orientation: Has helped scale a platform, portfolio, business, or comparable organization and understands what is required to move from entrepreneurial success to greater scale. Sees opportunity, identifies what is missing, and builds the capabilities to get there. Collaborative Leadership: Brings confidence, curiosity, humility, and sound judgment. Builds trust, offers intellectual debate, works effectively across a highly collaborative organization, and translates strategy into execution. Profit + Purpose: Believes strong financial performance and community impact can reinforce one another and is energized by the opportunity to build an investment platform that creates both economic and community impact. Passion for Chicago + Growth Mindset: Shares DL3's conviction in Chicago and is energized by the opportunity to help shape the city's next chapter. While the ideal candidate does not need to come from Chicago, they should be eager to become deeply connected to its business, civic, and community landscape. They will also recognize the opportunity to extend DL3's model and expertise to create impact in other markets over time. Location, Compensation and Benefits The position is based in Chicago, Illinois. review_candidates.title: Cost Accountant
review_candidates.description: Remote Raven is hiring a Cost Accountant on behalf of a long-established commercial electrical contractor headquartered in Arizona. The company builds complex electrical systems on healthcare, mission-critical/data-center, industrial, and commercial projects across the state and works with major national general contractors. Multiple projects run in parallel; each has its own budget, schedule of values, change-order activity, and life cycle to close out. This role sits inside the accounting team and pairs directly with project management on the money side of each job. You will monitor job costs, track budgets, analyze variances, prepare work-in-progress schedules, and reconcile project cost detail to the general ledger. You will be part of the monthly job cost review with project managers, and you will flag risks and overruns early so leadership can act on them. The role calls for someone who is confident in construction accounting mechanics — WIP, percentage-of-completion, committed costs, change orders — and who can explain those mechanics in plain language to non-accountants. Key Responsibilities Job Cost Monitoring & Budget Management Collaborate with project managers to develop and maintain detailed project budgets and financial forecasts. Track and analyze all job costs across each project life cycle, including labor, materials, equipment, and subcontractor expenses. Monitor change orders end-to-end and ensure accurate documentation, pricing, and budget adjustments are reflected in the ERP. Maintain accurate records of purchasing, vendor contracts, and committed costs on each active project. Financial Reporting & Variance Analysis Prepare monthly job cost reports and variance analyses for management review. Participate in monthly job cost meetings with the Project Management team, identifying variances and recommending corrective actions. Assist in preparing WIP schedules and contribute to monthly financial statement preparation. Review project billing and revenue recognition to ensure compliance with company policies and contract standards. General Ledger Reconciliation & Data Accuracy Reconcile project costs with general ledger accounts; ensure data accuracy across all financial systems. Maintain the integrity of project cost data through consistent data entry standards and regular reconciliation reviews. Identify and resolve discrepancies between project-level cost tracking and GL records. Audit Support & Internal Controls Support internal and external audits with detailed cost documentation, reconciliations, and organized project records. Continuously evaluate and improve cost tracking methods, accounting processes, and financial controls. Ensure the company’s cost accounting practices remain compliant with contract requirements and accounting standards. Cross-Functional Collaboration Work closely with Project Management as the financial counterpart to project leadership. Communicate financial insights, budget status, and cost concerns clearly to non-financial team members. Proactively flag financial risks, cost overruns, or budget anomalies to accounting leadership and project management. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field. Three or more years of cost accounting experience, preferably in construction or electrical contracting. Strong understanding of construction job cost accounting, WIP schedules, and percentage-of-completion revenue recognition. Proficiency in a construction accounting platform such as CMIC, Viewpoint Vista, Sage 300 CRE (Timberline), or a comparable system. Advanced Excel skills for financial modeling, variance analysis, and reporting. Excellent attention to detail, organization, and problem-solving. Clear and effective written English. Comfortable working independently in a remote environment. Overlap with US Mountain Standard Time business hours (Arizona does not observe DST). Preferred Qualifications Direct experience in electrical contracting, commercial construction, or specialty-trades accounting. CPA or CMA certification (or local equivalent). Experience managing job cost reporting across multiple simultaneous projects. Background supporting monthly close and WIP schedule preparation in construction. Tools & Software Construction Accounting Platform (primary): CMIC, Viewpoint Vista, Sage 300 CRE (Timberline), or comparable. Microsoft Excel — advanced. General Ledger / ERP modules for construction. Microsoft Teams, OneDrive, and video conferencing for remote coordination. What Makes You a Great Fit You understand how money moves through a construction project — and you catch cost problems before they become budget problems. Your WIP schedules and job cost reports are accurate and ready for management review without cleanup. Project Managers trust you because you make financial information clear and actionable. You are comfortable being the financial eyes on projects from a distance. You bring discipline and consistency to cost tracking. What We Offer Up to $9/hour 100% remote work Full-time role We hire for the long haul, so a steady track record of staying and growing always moves you up our list. To apply: Ensure your LinkedIn profile and resume are up-to-date and comprehensive (submit a comprehensive resume in English, PDF format), and complete the assessment in this link: [Aptive Test] — https://assessment.aptiveindex.com/s/0zhaJ9xfpL3F By applying, you consent to being contacted via the contact information provided in your application for recruitment purposes only. Because of the volume of applications we receive, we’re only able to follow up directly with candidates whose experience closely matches this role. If you don’t hear from us within 10 days, please know we genuinely appreciate your interest—and we’d welcome your application to future openings that may be a stronger fit. Thank you for considering Remote Raven, and all the best in your search. A note on scheduling: initial interviews run in US Mountain Standard Time (MST) within a 3:00 AM – 1:00 PM MST window. We know that takes flexibility around the time difference, and we genuinely appreciate it.

review_candidates.title: Chief Executive Officer - Phi Kappa Tau
review_candidates.job_function: Business Development, Education, and General Business
review_candidates.description: Organization Overview: Phi Kappa Tau Fraternity Phi Kappa Tau is entering an exciting period of growth and opportunity, as it builds on a 120-year tradition of championing brotherhood, learning, ethical leadership, and exemplary character. The fraternity serves 4,300 undergraduate members at approximately 80 chapters, and has about 100,000 alumni members. While the Phi Kappa Tau fraternity experience begins on campus, it lasts a lifetime: throughout their lives, members form meaningful friendships, find opportunities to lead and serve, and build powerful personal and professional networks. Phi Kappa Tau Fraternity (the Fraternity) is a 501(c)(7) nonprofit headquartered in Oxford, Ohio with a national staff of approximately 15 professionals and an elected Board, known as the National Council. It supports campus chapters and members with leadership development, educational programming, recruitment, chapter operations, national events, and alumni programs. The Fraternity is funded from undergraduate member fees, event registration fees, and an educational grant from the Phi Kappa Tau Foundation (the Foundation). The Foundation is an affiliated 501(c)(3) tax-exempt nonprofit organization with its own Board of Trustees and professional staff. The Fraternity collaborates with the Foundation on communications, events, alumni programming, and other areas where the two organizations have shared interests. In its next phase of growth, the Fraternity’s strategic plan, Building the Phi Kappa Tau Experience , centers on strengthening existing chapters, expanding to new campuses, deepening undergraduate and alumni engagement, broadening leadership and learning opportunities, and creating greater value for members throughout their lives. This is a once-in-a-generation opportunity to help shape the Phi Kappa Tau member experience at a time when meaningful personal connection and ethical leadership are more valuable than ever before. The next CEO will bring Phi Kappa Tau’s recognized leadership education to a new generation of students while strengthening the bonds of brotherhood among all members. Position Summary: Chief Executive Officer Phi Kappa Tau seeks an energetic, growth-minded Chief Executive Officer to champion its mission, support its members, and lead the organization into its next era of impact. Reporting to the National Council, the CEO will lead the execution of the organization’s strategic plan and serve as a highly relational leader who is equally comfortable working both in and on the organization. They will build credibility across a diverse community, from undergraduate members and young staff to alumni volunteers and university administrators. Internally, the CEO will lead a national staff and oversee a complex organization with an annual budget of approximately $3 million. This leader will bring financial discipline and operational rigor, with particular attention to budgeting, forecasting, accounts receivable, and financial reporting. They will provide the mentorship, coaching, structure, and accountability needed to help both early career and experienced staff members grow and perform at a high level. Externally, the CEO will focus on growth and engagement across the Fraternity. They will help existing chapters grow and thrive while executing our strategy to expand to new campuses. As a strong trust-builder and communicator, they will strengthen relationships with university administrators, engage Phi Kappa Tau’s alumni, expand its volunteer network, and create more opportunities for lifelong connection to the Fraternity. The ideal candidate will bring an appreciation for fraternity and lifelong brotherhood and exposure to collegiate fraternal organizations – whether through membership, professional leadership, volunteer service, or board involvement. Experience within business, membership organizations, or nonprofits is likewise valued. This is an opportunity to pair seasoned leadership with fresh thinking to shape the future of Phi Kappa Tau for generations to come. Key responsibilities Strategic Leadership, Governance & Growth Partner with the National Council on strategy, policy, and governance, providing timely reporting on organizational performance, finances, strategic plan progress, and emerging risks. Lead implementation of Phi Kappa Tau’s strategic plan, establishing measurable goals and translating priorities into clear organizational and staff work plans. Develop and execute strategies to grow undergraduate membership, strengthen retention, and expand Phi Kappa Tau to new campuses. Identify, execute, and evaluate new programs and approaches that advance strategic priorities, using data to understand results and scale what works. Organizational, Financial & People Leadership Lead the Fraternity’s approximately 15-person staff, including org chart design, hiring, performance management, compensation, professional development, and mentorship of both early-career and experienced professionals. Provide overall financial stewardship, including annual budgeting, cash flow management, fee-setting for programs and membership, collections, balance sheet management, and ongoing financial performance monitoring. Strengthen organizational systems and processes, using data and emerging technology (including AI) to improve efficiency, reporting, decision-making, and the member experience. Oversee proactive risk prevention, disciplinary issues, legal matters, and crisis response, stepping in directly to support chapters and volunteers when significant issues arise. Chapters, Members & Volunteers Ensure chapters receive responsive, high-quality support and resources that help them recruit and retain members, develop leaders, and operate effectively. Build and sustain Phi Kappa Tau’s volunteer network by recruiting and engaging volunteers, matching individuals with meaningful opportunities, and supporting volunteer boards and committees. Oversee national events and educational programming, including National Convention and leadership and learning programs. Improve the member experience by modernizing existing programs, services, communications, and digital resources, and finding innovative new ways to create value for undergraduate and alumni members. External Relations, Communications & Partnerships Serve as a visible public face and ambassador for Phi Kappa Tau at chapter, alumni, national, and interfraternal events and within the broader fraternity and sorority community. Strengthen relationships with host colleges and universities, including direct engagement with administrators when chapters need support or challenges arise. Partner with the Foundation Executive Director on joint initiatives and collaborative planning. Lead consistent, transparent, multi-channel communication with undergraduate members, alumni, volunteers, parents, university partners, and other stakeholders. Leadership & Competency Expectations Dynamic Communicator & Trusted Bridge-Builder An engaging leader who can connect authentically across the Phi Kappa Tau community. They will adapt their style to different audiences, listen with empathy, and skillfully navigate difficult conversations, whether navigating sensitive issues, supporting a chapter leader through a challenge, or advocating for the fraternity’s interests. A compelling storyteller and ambassador, they can also command a room, inspire new members, and represent Phi Kappa Tau with confidence before a range of audiences. Coach, Mentor & Team Builder Leads with a coaching mindset, creating an environment where a small, relatively young staff can learn, take ownership, and pursue ambitious goals. This leader will recognize that some team members are early in their careers and will provide the mentorship, feedback, professional development, and clear expectations the staff needs to succeed. They will build accountability while fostering a culture of trust, collaboration, and shared purpose. Innovative & Growth-Minded Leader Brings fresh thinking to how Phi Kappa Tau grows and creates meaningful value for its members. This leader will challenge longstanding approaches and critically evaluate processes, resources, and programs with an eye toward what today’s students and alumni need. They will strengthen existing chapters, expand to new campuses, and explore ways to diversify revenue sources. Decisive, Adaptable & Collaborative Leader Comfortable leading within a complex environment where decision-making involves varied stakeholders: student members, alumni, elected leadership, volunteers, and university administrators. This leader will listen to different perspectives and build buy-in while also knowing when it is time to make a decision and move forward. They are comfortable recognizing gaps in expertise and leveraging volunteers and outside experts. They will be responsive and consistent in their follow-through, working effectively with the National Council and volunteer leaders while navigating change and competing priorities. Location, Compensation and Benefits Phi Kappa Tau’s headquarters is located in Oxford, Ohio, and the organization welcomes candidates based in or around the Greater Cincinnati area. There is a strong preference for a CEO who can maintain a regular and visible presence in the Executive Offices, working alongside the staff and providing in-person mentorship, particularly to early-career team members. The role includes regular travel of approximately 10 - 25% to engage with chapters, members, alumni, volunteers, university partners, and attend national events, as well as occasional evening and weekend commitments. Salary is commensurate with experience and qualifications. Phi Kappa Tau offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental and vision coverage, paid time off, employer-paid life and disability insurance, and a 401(k) plan with an employer match.

Additional tasks as the role grows. What We're Looking For Two or more years in an executive assistant or customer service roles. Excellent written and spoken English. review_candidates.title: Event Operations Manager
review_candidates.description: Role: Event Operations Manager Location: Remote (LATAM-based welcome), with regular travel to the United States required to support on-site events ABOUT COSIGN Cosign is the fastest growing prop-tech company in the United States revolutionizing the $4 trillion rental industry with a market-leading one-of-a-kind rent guarantee product. Our mission is to expand housing access for renters and boost occupancy for landlords. Backed by top entrepreneurs, venture capital firms, and real estate investors, Cosign is built by experienced landlords and managers for landlords and managers who deeply understand the rental market’s needs. OUR MISSION CONTINUED Cosign is on a mission to expand access to housing by helping landlords approve more qualified renters - without increasing risk. We partner with owners and property managers to close the qualification gap caused by conditional approvals, thin credit files, and the absence of guarantors, materially improving leasing conversion and occupancy. We’re building toward a near future where every U.S. property offers Cosign to renters who struggle to qualify - expanding housing choice while helping owners and operators convert demand into signed leases. OUR HIRING PHILOSOPHY At Cosign, we seek exceptional talent with relentless intellectual curiosity - individuals who: • Challenge the status quo and drive continuous improvement • Demand excellence from themselves and their colleagues • Identify and solve problems others don't even recognize • Create innovative solutions others believe impossible We deliberately seek these rare, high-impact performers who attract similar talent. While most companies avoid hiring these exceptional individuals due to their demanding nature, we actively pursue them. When we find someone extraordinary, we move quickly to bring them onboard. We believe average talent builds average companies. By assembling a team of exceptional performers, we're creating the talent density needed to transform the rental industry and set new standards of excellence. THE OPPORTUNITY Calling all logistics obsessives and client-experience builders. We are looking for a hands-on, detail-driven, and proactive Event Operations Manager to own end-to-end logistics for our client-facing events and travel program from the ground up, supporting 100+ events per year. This is a founding operations role where you will own every piece of getting the team where they need to be, prepared, and ready to represent Cosign in front of clients and partners. As the first dedicated hire in this seat, you will own the entire stack: travel booking, event calendaring, agenda communication, client dinners and activities, booth installation and supervision, partner billing coordination, and ad-hoc gifting. You will work directly with Sales Operations and leadership to turn client-facing events into a well-oiled, high-touch operation, with every event tied to a seamless client experience. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a startup environment, has run high-volume event and travel logistics before, is comfortable owning vendor and partner relationships end-to-end, and is excited to own this function in a fast-moving, early-stage context. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES • Own the events and travel logistics engine across the business: booking flights, hotels, and rental cars for team members attending 100+ events per year, well ahead of each event date. • Maintain a rolling calendar of all events, tracking booking deadlines, confirmations, and any changes, and sending the team a clear pre-event agenda ahead of every event. • Coordinate directly with the Sales Operations team to align event logistics with account and pipeline priorities. • Serve as the point person for all client-related activities - every client touchpoint at an event runs through this role. • Plan and facilitate company events, activities and dinners end-to-end, including setting up invites via Luma/Partiful. • Evaluate restaurant options and activity ideas for client dinners and outings, balancing quality, location, and budget. • Correspond with partner companies on billing and logistics for co-hosted or co-sponsored events. • Own ad-hoc client and team gifting end-to-end - sourcing, ordering, and ensuring timely delivery. • A function that flexes with the business: stepping into adjacent client-experience and ad hoc projects as needed in an early-stage, fast-moving environment. • Maintain a detailed, structured expenditure ledger to ensure seamless financial reconciliation with the accounting team. ABOUT YOU As a highly organized and detail-driven Event Operations Manager, you take full ownership of events, travel, and accommodations, from initial booking through final send-off, without needing direction. You are deeply committed to getting every detail right, remain structured under pressure, and never let a booking deadline or client touchpoint slip. You thrive in early-stage landscapes where processes are still evolving. Instead of seeing gaps as obstacles, you view them as chances to build better systems, bring fresh ideas, and find energy in constructing something new rather than simply working inside it. You are a logistics and client-experience wizard, comfortable running multiple bookings and events at once, owning vendor and partner relationships, and making sure every client interaction feels seamless and well thought out. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE We are looking for a passionate, experienced operator who is excited about building a client-events function that has never been built before. • 3+ years of experience in event planning, travel coordination, executive support, or client experience roles; startup, proptech, fintech, or insurtech experience is a plus but not necessary • Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent bookings and deadlines without dropping details • Comfortable owning vendor and partner relationships, including billing and invoicing conversations • Strong written communication - comfortable sending clear, well-organized agendas and updates to a team • Experience with event platforms like Luma or Partiful, or similar tools, is a plus • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and calm under pressure when plans change last minute • Willingness to travel frequently, including internationally, to support on-site events • Must have current authorization to travel to the United States (e.g., a valid U.S. visitor visa or visa-free entry eligibility), and be able to maintain that authorization, as regular U.S. travel is a core requirement of this role WHAT MAKES THIS OPPORTUNITY DIFFERENT This is an opportunity to join one of the fastest-growing companies in U.S. PropTech at a pivotal moment in our growth. You will play a direct role in shaping how Cosign shows up for clients and partners in person, helping housing providers create better experiences for residents, renters, and property teams across the country. You will work alongside a team of exceptional performers, have direct access to senior leadership, and have real ownership over outcomes from day one. We move fast, we take care of our people, and we are building something that genuinely matters. WORKING AT COSIGN This is a remote position, with regular travel to the United States required to support major on-site events throughout the year. Cosign is looking for someone who is comfortable operating with pace, accountability, and a high degree of ownership. The right person will be energized by the opportunity to build structure within a growing business and create a lasting impact on how its client events run.

The CE Manager will ensure the effective and efficient operation, maintenance, and repair of all U.S.-owned and occupied facilities, infrastructure, and associated equipment in accordance with the base support contract Performance Work Statement (PWS). This position requires a broad technical background, strong project management capabilities, and a comprehensive understanding of contractual requirements and safety standards. Duties and Responsibilities: Overall Management & Supervision: Reports directly to the Program Manager and acts as the lead for all Civil Engineering activities. Provides daily oversight and supervision of the O&M staff, ensuring professional and quality services are provided to the customer. Manages the local national technical team, develops work schedules, and prioritizes job assignments according to mission needs. Provides training and management for the CE Department, including ancillary training and Job Qualification Standards for each trade. Actively participates in safety meetings, planning sessions, and status updates. Reviews and updates Civil Engineering job plans. Project Management & Coordination: Coordinates special projects with the CE Project Manager, Program Manager, U.S. Government (USG), and Sub-Contractors to establish schedules, project scope, budgets, dependencies, and responsibilities. Prepares Project Requests and justifications for submission to the USG. Works with the USG to understand site-specific characteristics and contribute to long-term building plans. Ensures all project work is managed within established budget criteria and submits justifications with associated costs for unforeseen site conditions that impact project work. Provides timely communication to the USG and interested parties regarding project progress, labor issues, material problems, and quality or code issues. Infrastructure & Facilities Maintenance: Maintains, repairs, constructs, and operates all U.S.-owned infrastructure to ensure reliable mission support. Oversees the maintenance of storm water drainage systems, pavements, walkways, and pads. Manages the maintenance of U.S.-controlled airfield navigation and lighting systems, airfield markings, and all associated utility services. Manages the complete facility maintenance program, including inspections, finishes, plumbing, HVAC, electrical, and roofing systems. Ensures all work and specifications comply with the Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC), National Fire Protection Association (NFPA), U.S. and International codes (electrical, plumbing, structural), and U.S. and European safety standards. Oversees the department's Tool Control Program and ensures accountability of all section assets. Reporting & Administration: Prepares and submits detailed reports, including monthly activities, work order status, chemical inventory, quarterly organization fuel tank usage, annual facility condition, and real property inventory reports. Inspects and audits in-process and completed work to ensure it meets PWS/SOW and quality standards. Updates and reviews information in the work order database (CMMS) and ensures site as-built drawings are updated following project completion. Coordinates with the Logistics Department for Requests for material, shop stock, and required equipment. Qualifications and Requirements: Education: Minimum of a Bachelor's degree in a discipline related to the contract requirement. An Associate's degree in Business Management or a similar discipline is preferred. Note: Two years of directly related experience is roughly equivalent to one year of formal education. Work Experience: A minimum of 3 to 10 years of experience in a discipline related to the contract requirement, with hands-on experience in a CE trade (e.g., generator maintenance, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, structures). Demonstrated 5 years of USAF or Civilian Base Civil Engineering knowledge and successful practice in implementing relevant regulations, manuals, and technical orders. 5 years of experience as a Supervisor in Operations and Maintenance and/or Project Management. 3-5 years of supervisory experience. Certifications & Clearances: Security Clearance: SECRET/T-3 U.S. Citizenship with an active passport and valid driver’s license. Journeyman trade-level certification(s) in HVAC and Electrical disciplines. Desired Certifications: Fire Suppression Systems Maintenance, GSA Locksmith, Backflow Prevention. Skills and Knowledge: Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office products (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Teams). Ability to prepare and interpret flowcharts, schedules, and step-by-step action plans. Solid organizational, multitasking, and time-management skills. Familiarity with risk management and quality assurance control principles. Knowledgeable in construction methods, technology, safety, and scheduling. Strong client-facing, teamwork, and communication skills, with experience leading diverse teams. Physical Requirements: Must be able to lift, pull, push, and carry up to 45 lbs. Other Responsibilities Safety - Amentum enforces a safety culture whereby all employees have the responsibility for continuously developing and maintaining a safe work environment. As appropriate, each employee is responsible for completing all training requirements and fulfilling all self-aid/buddy aid responsibilities, participating in emergency response tasks, and serving on safety committees and teams. It is our policy to consistently provide services that meet customer expectations. Accordingly, each employee must conform to the Amentum Quality Policy and carry out job activities in compliance with applicable Amentum Quality System documents and customer contracts. Each employee must read and understand his/her Quality Management and Customer Satisfaction responsibilities. Procedure Compliance - Each employee must read, understand, and implement the general and specific operational, safety, quality and environmental requirements of all plans, procedures and policies pertaining to job. Must be able to obtain and maintain a Secret US Government Clearance. Note: US Citizenship is required to obtain a Secret Clearance.
