new_matches.title: MEL Advisor
new_matches.description: A propos de FHI 360: FHI 360 est une organisation à but non lucratif dédiée au développement humain qui s'engage à améliorer durablement les conditions de vie en proposant des solutions intégrées et adaptées au contexte local. Notre personnel comprend des experts dans les domaines de la santé, des menaces pour la santé publique, de l'éducation, de la nutrition, de l'environnement, du développement économique, de la société civile, de la jeunesse, de la recherche, de la technologie, de la communication et du marketing social, créant ainsi un ensemble unique de compétences pour relever les défis interdépendants du développement actuel. Le programme Global Health Security (GHS) du gouvernement américain (USG) fournit une aide vitale pour prévenir, détecter et répondre aux menaces de maladies infectieuses qui présentent des risques pour la santé publique et pourraient coûter des vies. Dans le cadre du programme GHS de l'USG, l'activité Strengthening Infectious disease Détection Systems (STRIDES) fait progresser les efforts intersectoriels visant à identifier, gérer et répondre avec succès aux menaces de maladies infectieuses, à détecter et prévenir de nouvelles épidémies, et à instaurer la confiance dans les structures et les services de détection et de surveillance des maladies d'un pays. À Madagascar, STRIDES contribue également au renforcement des systèmes de surveillance et de réponse en lien avec la santé maternelle, néonatale et infantile (MNCH), notamment en matière de mortalité et de nutrition, ainsi qu’au soutien des efforts d’éradication de la poliomyélite, à travers l’intégration des activités de surveillance, d’investigation et de riposte, conformément aux priorités de la sécurité sanitaire mondiale. Résumé du poste : Le conseiller en suivi, évaluation et apprentissage (MEL Advisor) fournit des conseils techniques sur tous les aspects MEL de l'activité STRIDES (renforcement des systèmes de détection des maladies infectieuses) en Madagascar, notamment en supervisant l'exécution des activités MEL quotidiennes, en élaborant et en mettant en œuvre des politiques et des processus, et en garantissant la qualité des services fournis à l'aide des données du projet afin d'assurer une prise de décision fondée sur des preuves. Il/elle dirigera les activités visant à développer, opérationnaliser, mettre en œuvre et gérer les systèmes, outils et procédures MEL afin de collecter, compiler, analyser, interpréter et utiliser les données qui démontrent l'impact, la responsabilité et les progrès de l'activité. Le conseiller MEL supervisera directement le STRIDES MEL Officer et indirectement le personnel technique et les sous-traitants au niveau national afin de s'assurer que les activités menées dans le pays sont conformes aux objectifs du plan de travail et au plan MEL de l'activité (AMELP) et, par extension, aux priorités du gouvernement américain, et qu'elles sont mises en œuvre avec la plus grande qualité, dans les délais et dans les limites du budget. De plus, le titulaire de ce poste travaillera en étroite collaboration avec le personnel de PATH, sous-partenaire de STRIDES, basé à Madagascar. Le conseiller MEL fera la promotion de STRIDES en tant que leader d'opinion au sein de la communauté MEL en Côte d'Ivoire, contribuant ainsi au leadership éclairé de FHI 360 dans ce domaine grâce à la documentation des meilleures pratiques. Responsabilités: Soutenir la conception, le développement, la planification, la mise en œuvre et le reporting du plan AMELP de STRIDES. Développer, opérationnaliser, mettre en œuvre et gérer les systèmes, outils et procédures MEL afin de collecter, compiler, analyser, interpréter et utiliser les données qui démontrent l'impact, la responsabilité et les progrès des activités. Suivre les progrès du programme STRIDES par rapport aux indicateurs et aux objectifs MEL afin d'assurer un suivi et un reporting cohérents et systématiques. Veiller à ce que les plans MEL pertinents intègrent des méthodes quantitatives et qualitatives de haute qualité et des méthodologies participatives afin de contrôler la qualité des projets en termes de performances et de résultats. Évaluer les données et les efforts de reporting des sous-traitants en matière de MEL afin d'en vérifier la qualité. Renforcer les capacités du personnel de STRIDES en matière de MEL, notamment en renforçant, gérant et mettant en œuvre les systèmes MEL, en assurant la qualité des données, en facilitant l'apprentissage et l'échange de connaissances, en documentant les leçons apprises et les meilleures pratiques, et en établissant des rapports. Diriger les activités d'apprentissage et l'initiative d'utilisation des données de STRIDES ; favoriser une culture d'apprentissage et de partage des connaissances. Gérer les relations dans le pays avec les homologues des gouvernements nationaux, régionaux et locaux et les partenaires multisectoriels dans le domaine du MEL ; identifier le soutien technique nécessaire pour atteindre les objectifs nationaux en matière de sécurité sanitaire mondiale et de MEL. Diriger l'élaboration de plans et de budgets MEL spécifiques à chaque pays, alignés sur les objectifs de STRIDES et garantissant la conformité avec les politiques et procédures des donateurs et de l'organisation. Identifier et consulte l'équipe de direction de STRIDES sur les recommandations visant à améliorer la mise en œuvre et les résultats des activités. Superviser et encadrer le personnel ; supervise les processus de recrutement, d'embauche et d'intégration selon les besoins. Soutenir la gestion des performances et le développement professionnel des subordonnés directs, notamment par le biais de retours d'information réguliers, de coaching et d'accompagnement de carrière. Accomplir d'autres tâches qui lui sont assignées. Connaissances et compétences appliquées : Connaissance approfondie et expérience des mécanismes dans le domaine des pratiques nationales et internationales en matière de suivi, d'évaluation et d'apprentissage (MEL). Capacité à gérer des projets, à établir des priorités réalistes et à planifier la mise en œuvre réussie des activités. Excellentes compétences en communication orale et écrite ; maîtrise d'une deuxième langue (français, espagnol et/ou russe) souhaitable. Excellentes compétences organisationnelles et analytiques. Leadership technique et en matière de projets démontré. Capacité à motiver, influencer et bien travailler avec les autres pour atteindre les objectifs de STRIDES. Capacité à échanger des informations, à présenter des recommandations et à collaborer avec des collègues et des pairs au sein de STRIDES et à l'extérieur, selon les besoins. Capacité à convaincre les autres des avantages/de l'importance d'une idée ou d'un plan d'action et à obtenir leur soutien ou leur engagement. Solides compétences en matière de négociation et capacité à parvenir à des points d'accord et à des avantages mutuels entre pairs et collègues. Capacité à établir des relations de travail positives avec diverses communautés de parties prenantes, des représentants gouvernementaux et d'autres organismes multilatéraux et représentants de donateurs. Solides compétences organisationnelles, grand souci du détail et efficacité dans le respect des délais. Compétences : Il existe beaucoup des compétences de développement FHI 360, les plus axées pour ce poste particulier seront : Gestion de projet (planification et gestion du temps) Définir précisément la durée et la difficulté des tâches (définir objectifs/objectifs/mesures). Divise le travail en étapes, plannings, tâches et affectations de personnes. Organise efficacement les personnes, le temps et les ressources. Organise l'information de manière utile et orchestre plusieurs activités en même temps. Gestion des Personnes (Rendre les Autres Grands) Faciliter le développement professionnel du personnel en proposant des missions et opportunités stimulantes et apprenantes. Il partage et sollicite des retours au moins chaque mois. Aide à établir des plans de développement convaincants. Attribue la responsabilité et la responsabilité des tâches/décisions. Surveille le processus, l'avancement et les résultats. Cela crée un climat où les gens veulent donner le meilleur d'eux-mêmes. Création et gestion de systèmes et de processus. Reconnaît la nécessité de normalisation et équilibre les besoins du client et de l'organisation dans la conception des systèmes. Anticipe les effets du changement de processus sur les personnes tout en optimisant l'efficacité et la simplicité des tâches. Les employés sont censés posséder ou avoir un fort potentiel pour le développement de ces trois compétences fondamentales. Résolution de problèmes et impact : Démontre la capacité d'évaluer les besoins dans le cadre des devoirs convenus et considère la meilleure marche à suivre pour répondre à ces besoins. new_matches.description: Job Description Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. In order to contribute to this result, the UN Women Regional Office for the Americas and the Caribbean, in collaboration with the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID) implements the project "Transforming economies. Towards the Recognition, Reduction and Redistribution of Unpaid Domestic and Care Work in Latin America and the Caribbean". The objective of the project is to increase the economic autonomy and well-being of women in Latin America through their access to comprehensive care policies and systems. To this end, at the regional level, the project works on the generation of applicable knowledge and public positioning on comprehensive care policies and systems in Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC). At the national level, the project is implemented in Peru, Ecuador, Mexico, Panama and the Dominican Republic, strengthening national and local capacities to provide care services and infrastructures at the national and subnational level as an impetus towards the construction of a National Care System, placing special emphasis on the generation of inspiring practices at the local level. Likewise, in its mission, the project seeks to strengthen bi-regional cooperation between Latin America and the Caribbean with Europe, taking advantage of the impulse that feminist foreign policy in both regions is giving to the development of comprehensive care policies and systems. Under the guidance and direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director, the Regional Programme Specialist will be responsible for providing strategic leadership and comprehensive management of the care program. The incumbent will substantively and operationally coordinate the implementation of programmed care activities, ensure effective articulation between the different components of the project, and ensure the achievement of results and implementation of activities in accordance with the Project Document approved by UN Women and the donor and other applicable reference documents. The Regional Programme Specialist will work closely with the economic empowerment team, specifically the technical care specialists and operations team of the UN Women regional office, as well as the economic empowerment teams of the UN Women country offices in Latin America and the Caribbean. Likewise, in coordination with UN Women's country offices, the incumbent will maintain communication with national and local partner institutions to ensure the implementation of the activities foreseen in the project in the prioritized countries and contribute to the development of regional activities and the achievement of results. Availability is required for travel within Latin America and the Caribbean. Key Functions and Accountabilities : Lead the implementation of the project "Transforming economies. Towards the Recognition, reduction and redistribution of unpaid domestic and care work in Latin America and the Caribbean" at the LAC regional level Lead the implementation of activities developed under the regional component of the care project, ensuring high standards of quality and efficiency and fostering synergies between regional, national, and local components. This includes the coordination, monitoring and substantive review of the products and actions developed in the field of care. Lead strategic project planning and collaborate with country offices to develop and implement Annual Work Plans, evaluating progress, budget execution and results, and providing technical guidance for efficient management. Establish and strengthen coordination mechanisms between the countries involved in the program and the levels of work, including the subnational level (local governments, civil society, among others), to ensure fluid communication and effective articulation of actions; Contribute to the establishment and strengthening of strategic alliances with institutional partners and key actors, create synergies with other donor initiatives in the region, and broaden the base of collaboration through consultation and mapping processes of relevant actors in the care agenda. Facilitate inter-agency relations between UN Women and its partners through planning, coordination, and active participation in dialogue spaces such as technical meetings, workshops, field missions, and other related events; Maintain a channel of permanent consultation and coordination with the technical teams of the country offices, the specialized technical advisors, the UN Women regional team, national and/or local partners and the donor, to contribute to the articulated implementation of the project activities; Coordinate the organization and governance mechanisms of the Project (Regional Steering Committee, National Steering Committee and Operational Working Group) and provide relevant technical inputs such as presentations, key data, executive reports and supporting documentation; Collaborate in the implementation of communication and advocacy strategies to make visible the results of the project and the work of UN Women in care, providing technical inputs for communication products, and defend the care agenda in key spaces at the regional level; Lead the design and implementation of the project's monitoring and evaluation strategy, develop tools for monitoring results and indicators, evaluate the impact of activities, and oversee the preparation of technical and financial reports in accordance with UN Women and donor standards. Provide technical advisory support on UN Women's actions in the field of care at the regional level within the framework of the care project in LAC. Provide specialized technical advice to country offices, government partners, and civil society organizations to develop and/or strengthen care systems, policies, frameworks, and strategies in the region. Develop context analysis, programmatic proposals, and methodological tools that contribute to evidence-based policymaking, as well as resource mobilization around the care agenda. Collaborate in the organization and facilitation of spaces for dialogue, meetings and face-to-face and virtual workshops, aimed at different strategic actors, in order to expand the processes of training, learning and articulation in the region. Manage the production and review of technical knowledge (policy documents, guides, case studies, tools, etc.), and evaluate experiences developed by UN Women in the region, ensuring their articulation with the regional care agenda. Create mechanisms for dialogue and participation with key actors to defend the political and technical commitment to the implementation of comprehensive care systems, in line with the Tlatelolco Commitment and other regional initiatives. Manage the development of partnerships and resource mobilization as it relates to the care project in LAC. Facilitate knowledge building and sharing within the framework of the care project in LAC. Support and oversee the reporting and produce regional analysis including global trends and identifying challenges. Lead the development and dissemination of good practices and lessons learned on coordination and gender mainstreaming. Provide capacity development support to regional and country level colleagues on coordination mandate and gender mainstreaming. Develop capacity development initiatives on gender-related issues and priorities as needed. new_matches.title: Global Financial Shared Services Manager
new_matches.description: Job Summary The Global Financial Shared Services Manager will lead IPA's newly established Shared Services Center within the Global Finance team. The role is responsible for building the center from the ground up — designing processes, developing a team of up to five staff, and serving as the primary point of contact for country office finance teams and headquarters leadership. The Shared Services Manager will ensure timely, accurate, and compliant processing of accounts payable, journal entries, expense reports, intercompany transactions, and bank and balance sheet reconciliations across all IPA entities worldwide. Responsibilities Operations and Service Delivery Lead day-to-day operations of the Shared Services Center, covering accounts payable, journal entry processing, intercompany transactions, and bank and balance sheet reconciliations for all IPA offices. Establish and monitor service-level agreements (SLAs) with country offices and headquarters, including processing turnaround times, accuracy rates, and query resolution timelines. Coordinate with country office finance staff to resolve queries, address missing documentation, clear reconciliation discrepancies, and ensure completeness of month-end close activities. Provide coverage to country office finance teams during periods of staff transition. Support all offices with audit requests as needed. Process Design and Continuous Improvement Identify opportunities for automation, system improvements, and process simplification, and lead implementation in coordination with IT and Global Finance teams. Develop performance dashboards and key performance indicators (KPIs) for the Shared Services function, and report results to senior finance leadership on a regular cadence. Build team capacity to take on additional responsibilities with a consistent level of excellence. Team Leadership and Talent Development Recruit, onboard, and supervise a team of up to three Shared Services staff. Set individual performance objectives, conduct performance reviews, and support professional development. Design and deliver training for junior staff on accounting tasks, reconciliation procedures, NetSuite operations, and country-specific requirements; maintain training documentation for knowledge continuity. Monitor individual and team workload across country assignments; adjust capacity allocation and escalate resourcing needs proactively. Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Compliance and Controls Ensure all transactions comply with IPA policies, donor requirements, and relevant accounting standards. Support internal and external audits by providing required documentation. Maintain clear segregation of duties between the Shared Services Center and country office banking and treasury functions. Stakeholder Engagement and Reporting Serve as the primary liaison between the Shared Services Center, country office finance teams, and headquarters Global Finance. Oversee generation of monthly financial reports for distribution to country office finance teams and leadership. Lead regular check-ins and reporting meetings with country office finance leads, providing updates on month-end close status, outstanding issues, and team performance. Communicate process changes, training requirements, and service updates to all stakeholders. Contribute to cross-functional projects related to finance transformation and other global initiatives as needed. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in accounting or finance. Minimum seven years of progressive experience in accounting, including at least three years of direct supervisory experience. Demonstrated experience leading or working in a shared services, business process outsourcing (BPO), or centralized finance environment. Full professional proficiency in English and Spanish, written and spoken. Strong working knowledge of accounts payable processes, general ledger accounting, and internal controls. Proficiency with ERP systems, preferably NetSuite, and advanced Microsoft Excel skills. Proven ability to collaborate across time zones and cultures, with strong written and verbal communication skills. Experience supporting multi-currency and multi-country accounting operations. Certified Public Accountant (CPA), Chartered Accountant (CA), or equivalent professional certification. (preferred) Master's degree in accounting, finance, or business administration. (preferred) Experience with nonprofit, international development, or donor-funded organizations, including familiarity with USG and FCDO requirements. (preferred) Demonstrated experience designing or improving accounting processes across multiple entities or geographies. (preferred) Location This role may be based in any IPA office, provided a high level of overlap with other offices' time zones. Reports To Global Controller (Headquarters) Application Deadline 1 Oct 2026 About IPA Innovations for Poverty Action (IPA) is a research and policy nonprofit that discovers and advances what works to improve the lives of people living in poverty. IPA brings together researchers and decision-makers to design, rigorously evaluate, and refine these solutions and their applications, ensuring that the evidence created is used to improve the lives of people living in poverty. In recent decades, trillions of dollars have been spent on programs designed to reduce global poverty, but clear evidence of which programs succeed is rare, and when evidence does exist, decision-makers often do not know about it. IPA exists to bring together leading researchers and these decision-makers to ensure that the evidence we create leads to a tangible impact on the world. Since its founding in 2002, IPA has worked with over 600 leading academics to conduct over 1,000 evaluations in 52 countries. This research has informed hundreds of successful programs that now impact millions of individuals worldwide. Safeguarding at IPA At Innovations for Poverty Action (IPA), we are committed to creating a safe and respectful environment for all individuals, particularly children and vulnerable adults. As IPA adheres to strict safeguarding principles, selected candidates will be expected to adhere to these standards. By joining IPA, you become part of a team dedicated to ethical conduct, social responsibility, and meaningful impact in the fight against global poverty. Together, we work to create a better world where everyone has the opportunity to thrive with dignity and respect.

This role sits inside the accounting team and pairs directly with project management on the money side of each job. You will monitor job costs, track budgets, analyze variances, prepare work-in-progress schedules, and reconcile project cost detail to the general ledger. You will be part of the monthly job cost review with project managers, and you will flag risks and overruns early so leadership can act on them. The role calls for someone who is confident in construction accounting mechanics — WIP, percentage-of-completion, committed costs, change orders — and who can explain those mechanics in plain language to non-accountants. Key Responsibilities Job Cost Monitoring & Budget Management Collaborate with project managers to develop and maintain detailed project budgets and financial forecasts. Track and analyze all job costs across each project life cycle, including labor, materials, equipment, and subcontractor expenses. Monitor change orders end-to-end and ensure accurate documentation, pricing, and budget adjustments are reflected in the ERP. Maintain accurate records of purchasing, vendor contracts, and committed costs on each active project. Financial Reporting & Variance Analysis Prepare monthly job cost reports and variance analyses for management review. Participate in monthly job cost meetings with the Project Management team, identifying variances and recommending corrective actions. Assist in preparing WIP schedules and contribute to monthly financial statement preparation. Review project billing and revenue recognition to ensure compliance with company policies and contract standards. General Ledger Reconciliation & Data Accuracy Reconcile project costs with general ledger accounts; ensure data accuracy across all financial systems. Maintain the integrity of project cost data through consistent data entry standards and regular reconciliation reviews. Identify and resolve discrepancies between project-level cost tracking and GL records. Audit Support & Internal Controls Support internal and external audits with detailed cost documentation, reconciliations, and organized project records. Continuously evaluate and improve cost tracking methods, accounting processes, and financial controls. Ensure the company’s cost accounting practices remain compliant with contract requirements and accounting standards. Cross-Functional Collaboration Work closely with Project Management as the financial counterpart to project leadership. Communicate financial insights, budget status, and cost concerns clearly to non-financial team members. Proactively flag financial risks, cost overruns, or budget anomalies to accounting leadership and project management. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field. Three or more years of cost accounting experience, preferably in construction or electrical contracting. Strong understanding of construction job cost accounting, WIP schedules, and percentage-of-completion revenue recognition. Proficiency in a construction accounting platform such as CMIC, Viewpoint Vista, Sage 300 CRE (Timberline), or a comparable system. Advanced Excel skills for financial modeling, variance analysis, and reporting. Excellent attention to detail, organization, and problem-solving. Clear and effective written English. Comfortable working independently in a remote environment. Overlap with US Mountain Standard Time business hours (Arizona does not observe DST). Preferred Qualifications Direct experience in electrical contracting, commercial construction, or specialty-trades accounting. CPA or CMA certification (or local equivalent). General Ledger / ERP modules for construction. Microsoft Teams, OneDrive, and video conferencing for remote coordination. What Makes You a Great Fit You understand how money moves through a construction project — and you catch cost problems before they become budget problems. new_matches.title: Executive Assistant
new_matches.description: About The Role Our client is a growing early education program with two campuses in Memphis, Tennessee. Families trust the center with their children, so every interaction has to feel warm, prompt, and professional. This role is the first voice a prospective family hears in writing. You own the path from a new inquiry to a booked tour, and you keep the daily back office running behind it. The work splits into two major areas. The first half is parent facing. You respond to inquiries, answer questions, schedule tours, and follow up until families are on the calendar. The second half is operational. You keep attendance, meal counts, menus, and ordering accurate and on time across both campuses. The owner is building the business and launching a nonprofit alongside it. This is a long-term role with room to take on more as trust is established. What You'll Do Monitor new parent inquiries as they arrive in ProCare our CRM & ERP system and respond immediately. Make first contact with every inquiry, answer initial questions, and move the family toward a campus tour. Book tours through Calendly and confirm each appointment with the parent. Follow up with leads who do not reply or do not book, using a consistent reminder sequence. Track inquiries and booked tours weekly and report the numbers. The standing target is at least five scheduled tours for every ten inquiries. Answer parent emails daily in a tone that reflects how the center treats its families. Enter daily attendance in ProCare for both campuses. Pull attendance from ProCare and maintain a combined attendance spreadsheet in Excel covering both campuses. Enter daily meal counts into the Kid Care food program using ProCare attendance. Breakfast at 8:55 a.m., lunch at 11:00 a.m., and afternoon snack at 2:30 p.m., for both campuses. Enter school menus into ProCare for both campuses. Add events, closures, and important dates to the center calendar. Create flyers in Canva for events, enrollment promotions, and parent announcements. Assist in all digital marketing efforts such as website updates, social media posts, simple video editing, etc. Place grocery and supply orders through Instacart and Performance Foodservice. Additional tasks as the role grows. What We're Looking For Two or more years in an executive assistant or customer service roles. Excellent written and spoken English. Parents will judge the school by your communication. A warm, professional communication style. First impressions carry weight in a business built on trust. Deadline driven with strong attention to detail. Attendance and meal counts are entered on time every day without reminders. Comfortable working toward a number and reporting on it honestly each week. Intermediate Excel skills, including sorting, filtering, basic formulas, and building clean summary sheets. Experience using a customer relationship management system to track leads and follow up. Highly reliable. Availability for live coordination during United States Central Time business hours. Nice to Have Experience in childcare, education, healthcare, or another service business built on client trust. Hands on experience with ProCare. Familiarity with food program reporting such as the Child and Adult Care Food Program. Canva design experience. Experience with online ordering platforms such as Instacart. Administrative support experience with a nonprofit organization. How This Role Works You report directly to the owner, who also serves as school director. The team is small, so you will have real ownership of the inquiry pipeline and the daily reporting from early on. You will not be answering the main center phone line. Communication happens through email, the customer relationship management system, and scheduled check ins. Onboarding is hands on at the start. You will be taught how this center operates. Expect to ask questions early, confirm details in writing, and give visibility into your work before anyone asks for it. Success in the first 90 days looks like this. By day 30, you handle new inquiries and book tours independently, and daily attendance and meal counts are entered on time, and the food menus. By day 60, you own the parent email inbox, the attendance spreadsheet, the calendar, and tour bookings are consistently at target. By day 90, you anticipate what is coming, run the recurring back-office processes without any prompting, and the owner spends measurably less time on follow-up and administration.

You thrive in early-stage landscapes where processes are still evolving. You are a logistics and client-experience wizard, comfortable running multiple bookings and events at once, owning vendor and partner relationships, and making sure every client interaction feels seamless and well thought out. The right person will be energized by the opportunity to build structure within a growing business and create a lasting impact on how its client events run.
